title: HomeFlood Cancellation: Share of the Premium Return After Recent Claims
content:
**Rule.** When a HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies policy is cancelled on the named insured's signed request, recent claim payments decide how much of the premium return is kept. The premium return here means the term-premium part and the loss-of-use part of the return, before any policy-fee return or exit fee.

The test reads the claim payments on the policy, net of voided payments, for losses dated fewer than 12 whole months before the processing date.

| Those net claim payments | Share of the premium return paid |
|---|---|
| more than zero and at least 25 percent of the dwelling limit and personal property limit taken together | nothing |
| more than zero but less than that | 50 percent |
| zero | all of it |

**The processing date.** The processing date is the day the cancellation is processed and recorded, and every window counted to the processing date ends on that day. A count of whole calendar months runs from the earlier date to the later one; the last month is not counted when the later date's day of the month falls before the earlier date's day of the month.

## Hypothetical cases

| Policy limits (dwelling plus personal property) | Net claim payments in the window | Share |
|---|---|---|
| 300,000 plus 100,000 (25 percent is 100,000) | 100,000.00 | nothing |
| 300,000 plus 100,000 | 12,500.00 | 50 percent |
| renters policy, 0 plus 40,000 (25 percent is 10,000) | 0 | all |
| renters policy, 0 plus 40,000 | 10,000.00 | nothing |
